title: Size Selection Protocol for Library Molecules
author: Dakota Betz
materials: The double-sided size selection protocol outlined in this appendix is designed for the selection of library molecules (inclusive of adapter) in the range of 250 – 450 bp. To obtain a population of shorter or longer molecules, the protocol may be modified as follows: A B C D 1 Upper size limit Modification Lower size limit Modification 2 Increase Decrease the ratio of the first cut Increase Decrease the ratio of the second cut* 3 Decrease Increase the ratio of the first cut Decrease Increase the ratio of the second cut* * The second size cut should be performed with at least 0.2 volumes of KAPA cleanup beads reagent. Please note that the volume of KAPA cleanup beads needed for the second cut is calculated relative to the volume of the DNA at the start of the size selection procedure, not the volume of the DNA-containing supernatant transferred after the first cut. DNA recovery is dramatically reduced if the difference between first and second cuts is less than ~0.2 volumes. To increase the amount of DNA recovered, >0.2 volumes of KAPA cleanup beads may be used for the second cut, but note that this may result in the recovery of smaller library fragments and/or a broader size distribution. For more information on double-sided size selection, please refer to the KAPA NGS Library Preparation Technical Guide (available on request from Technical Support at sequencing.roche.com/support).

steps.title: Set up first size cut
steps.instruction: Combine 50 µL DNA to be size selected with 35 µL KAPA cleanup beads (0.7X ratio) in each well or tube for a total volume of 85 µL.

steps.title: Bind large fragments
steps.instruction: Mix the reaction thoroughly by vortexing or pipetting up and down multiple times, incubate at room temperature for 5–15 minutes to allow binding of library molecules larger than ~450 bp to the beads, then place the plate/tube(s) on a magnetic rack and incubate until the liquid becomes clear.

steps.title: Collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully transfer approximately 80 µL of the clear supernatant (containing library molecules smaller than ~450 bp) to a new plate or tube, ensuring no beads are transferred, and discard the original plate/tube containing the beads.

steps.title: Set up second size cut
steps.instruction: Combine the 80 µL supernatant from the first cut with 10 µL KAPA cleanup beads (0.9X ratio) in each well or tube for a total volume of 90 µL.

steps.title: Bind medium fragments
steps.instruction: Mix thoroughly by vortexing or pipetting up and down multiple times, incubate at room temperature for 5–15 minutes to bind library molecules larger than ~250 bp to the beads, then place on a magnetic rack and incubate until the liquid is clear.

steps.title: Discard unwanted supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully remove and discard the supernatant, which contains library molecules smaller than ~250 bp.

steps.title: First ethanol wash
steps.instruction: While the plate/tube(s) remain on the magnet, add 200 µL of 80 % ethanol, then incubate at room temperature for at least 30 seconds.

steps.title: Second ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Again, while on the magnet, add another 200 µL of 80 % ethanol and incubate at room temperature for at least 30 seconds.

steps.title: Remove ethanol
steps.instruction: Carefully remove and discard the ethanol, trying to eliminate all residual ethanol without disturbing the beads.

steps.title: Dry beads
steps.instruction: Dry the beads at room temperature for 3–5 minutes or until all ethanol has evaporated; avoid over‑drying as it may reduce yield.

steps.title: Elute DNA
steps.instruction: Remove the plate/tube(s) from the magnet, thoroughly resuspend the beads in the required volume of elution buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 8.0–8.5), incubate at room temperature for 2 minutes to elute DNA, place the plate/tube(s) back on the magnet and incubate until the liquid is clear.

steps.title: Collect size‑selected DNA
steps.instruction: Transfer the clear supernatant containing the size‑selected DNA to a new plate or tube; proceed with downstream steps or store the DNA at 2 °C–8 °C for 1–2 weeks, or at –15 °C to –25 °C for longer term storage.
